description: We're PLAYTECH! A team of tech enthusiasts interested in exploring ideas, learning and building cool things. For this hackathon, we're creating an interactive space-outpost experience where players discover the challenges of surviving on the Moon or Mars. We're looking for curious, creative people with skills in programming, game development, UI/UX, design, science or research. You don't have to be an expert. Just bring your ideas, enthusiasm and willingness to build something awesome with us!
summary:
NEON RIFT: LUNAR FRONTIER is a 3D educational game developed by Team PlayTech for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It is designed to help young people understand the challenges of life and work on the Moon.

Players control three astronauts on a 14-day mission in a moon base. They explore the facilities, drive a rover, manage oxygen and electricity and make decisions when unexpected problems occur. Every activity demonstrates the significance of planning and teamwork when resources are scarce and every system counts.

Rather than just reading about lunar exploration, players can experience some of the challenges. We hope that NEON RIFT will make space science more interesting, encourage practical problem solving and inspire young students to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering and space exploration in the future.
details:
NEON RIFT: LUNAR FRONTIER is a 3D interactive game we have created to help young people understand the difficulties of living and working on the Moon.

You play as three astronauts on a 14 day mission exploring a lunar settlement while managing vital resources such as oxygen, electricity and food. The base consists of a habitat and six operational sectors where players perform duties, do research and respond to unexpected emergencies.

We made the game in Godot Engine with GDScript, a mix of 3D exploration, storytelling, resource management and interactive missions. AI tools were also used in the development and debugging.

We want to help make space science more accessible, to foster problem solving and collaboration, and to inspire young people to pursue careers in science and engineering.
